hypotheses.root_cause: A long power burst (30 W for 921 ms, starting at 1526 ms) used up the cooling headroom. The single DVFS step-down from 1200 to 1000 MHz was too small and came too late, so junction temperature passed the 105C trip point and reached 119C.
hypotheses.rationale: Sequence of events: THERMAL WARN at 95C with DVFS policy (1498 ms), then PMU 'Power burst detected p_w=30 dur_ms=921' (1526 ms), which is the catalogue tell-tale for RC_WORKLOAD_BURST. Next came one DVFS step-down to 1000 MHz (1684 ms). The burst was still running when the trip hit at 1997 ms (119C), followed by the FATAL shutdown at 2010 ms. I found no markers for the other candidates anywhere in the run (filtered 0–2010 ms): no 'fan speed below profile' / target_rpm line, which argues against RC_FAN_PROFILE_BAD, and no sensor-to-ambient delta_c line, which argues against RC_HEATSINK_POOR. Rail telemetry looks healthy (droop_cnt=0, VCORE 830–875 mV), so a regulator limit is unlikely. The closest past incident (run 000020, similarity 0.93) was also resolved as a workload burst. One thing doesn't fit neatly: before the trip, samples stayed between 93 and 97C, then jumped to 119C. That could just be gaps between samples, but a sensor or hotspot problem can't be fully ruled out, so I'm not putting confidence higher.
recommended_actions: Re-run the same test with burst power capped (e.g. PL2 limited to ~20-25 W) and confirm no trip with the same cooling setup
Make the DVFS reaction more aggressive: step down in more stages or bigger steps (e.g. to 800 MHz) when a burst is detected while above 95C, and shorten the policy reaction time
During the re-run, log fan RPM against target and the die-to-ambient delta to properly rule out fan-profile and heatsink causes
Sample the thermal sensors faster during bursts to explain the 97C to 119C jump and rule out a sensor or hotspot problem

Prior for THERMAL_TRIP: Junction temperature exceeded the thermal trip threshold
Temperature climbed past the DVFS policy and crossed the 105C trip point before throttling could recover it, triggering an emergency shutdown — a cooling-solution or fan-profile shortfall under sustained workload.

- RC_HEATSINK_POOR: Poor heatsink/TIM contact — large die-to-ambient delta
    tell-tales: sensor-to-ambient delta high, delta_c
    actions: Re-seat the heatsink and replace the TIM; Measure mounting pressure against the thermal spec
- RC_FAN_PROFILE_BAD: Fan speed stays below the profile target as temperature rises
    tell-tales: fan speed below profile, target_rpm
    actions: Fix the fan curve / PWM mapping in the thermal policy; Verify tachometer feedback and fan power
- RC_WORKLOAD_BURST: A sustained power burst outruns the cooling headroom
    tell-tales: power burst detected, p_w=
    actions: Cap the burst power or lengthen the DVFS step-down reaction; Add thermal headroom to the test's power envelope
